extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, and students considering submissions to the RTDNA Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for entering the Radio Television Digital News Association's Edward R. Murrow Awards, including eligibility divisions, category definitions, content/length limits, judging procedures, and student-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Murrow Awards recognize local and national news stories that uphold the RTDNA Code of Ethics, demonstrate technical expertise and exemplify the importance and impact of journalism as a service to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Murrow Award winning work demonstrates the excellence that Edward R. Murrow made a standard for the broadcast news profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and possibility of withholding awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are judged by a panel of professional journalists. Entries from individual stations are judged regionally; regional winners are entered into judging for the national awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National award winners are recognized each October. It is possible for the judges to decide that none of the entries in a given category merit an award, in which case none will be offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio Small Market eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Local radio stations located in markets 50+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media market sizes for radio are determined by Nielsen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio Large Market eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Local radio stations located in markets 1–50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media market sizes for radio are determined by Nielsen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television Small Market eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Local TV stations located in markets 50+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media market sizes for television are determined by Nielsen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television Large Market eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Local TV stations located in markets 1–50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media market sizes for television are determined by Nielsen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network Radio eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A radio network, syndication service, or program service that programs to multiple markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network-level entries are judged in their own division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network Television eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A television network, syndication service, or program service that programs to multiple markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network-level entries are judged in their own division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Digital News Organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital organizations with 2,499,999 or fewer unique visitors per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital divisions are defined by monthly unique visitor thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Digital News Organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital organizations with 2,499,999 or more unique visitors per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital divisions are defined by monthly unique visitor thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student division eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone enrolled in a high school, college or university in the United States, Canada or any other country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student awards (added 2015) are awarded to the individuals or team that produce them, unlike professional awards which are presented to a news organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Excellence (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry consists of up to 40 minutes of examples of the previous year's news coverage and then a single newscast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showcases a news organization's overall work across a year; submission is limited to the 40-minute examples plus one newscast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newscast (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: One regularly scheduled newscast from the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single complete newscast is submitted as the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Coverage / Spot News (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may consist of up to 20 minutes of examples of a station's coverage of a single, unscheduled news event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused on coverage of a single breaking event; time limit is 20 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Coverage (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may consist of up to 30 minutes of examples showing continuing coverage of a major developing story over an extended period of time during the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to demonstrate sustained reporting on a developing story; time limit is 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Reporting (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single report of up to 10 minutes covering a human-interest or profile subject that is not breaking news or investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on human-interest/profile storytelling; max length 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may consist of up to 15 minutes of examples of journalistic enterprise on an important issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should demonstrate investigative effort and impact; max length 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Documentary (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 60 minutes of coverage of a single subject reported in a single segment addressing a need or needs in the station's market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form single-segment documentary format; max length 60 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Series (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of a single subject reported in multiple parts, not to exceed 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-part reporting on a single subject with total time capped at 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard News Reporting (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single hard news report of up to 10 minutes prepared for a newscast that is not breaking news or primarily investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straight reporting prepared for newscasts; max length 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports Reporting (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single packaged report of up to 10 minutes covering a sports-related topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchored segments or stand-alone sports programs and play-by-play are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Sound (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10 minutes of coverage of a single subject or single segment showing creative use of sound to tell a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on creative and effective use of audio/sound design; max length 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Video (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry up to 10 minutes showing creative use of video to tell a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on visual storytelling and creative video techniques; max length 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to three examples from the previous year, not exceeding 15 minutes, that demonstrate excellence in writing that conveys the feeling and significance of events to the listener or viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit writing samples (readable/airable) that show narrative and explanatory skill; combined time limit 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia / Website (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 15 examples of URLs, including the news organization's home page, which demonstrate exceptional news coverage and journalistic skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should showcase digital storytelling across URLs and pages; formerly listed as 'Website'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Innovation (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 30 minutes of audio or video coverage, or URLs, apps, social feeds, or any other platform that demonstrates an innovative use of content, engagement, technology and/or audience experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New (2017) — focuses on novel uses of platforms, technology, and audience engagement; max 30 minutes of media or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Social Media (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10 examples of URLs, apps, or other platforms that demonstrate the exceptional use of social media as evidenced by the quality of journalism and the quantity and quality of user engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New (2017) — emphasizes journalistic quality plus measurable user engagement across social channels; submit up to 10 examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient rules (organization vs. individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edward R. Murrow Awards are presented to media organizations as a whole rather than to individual journalists; however, many categories are for single news reports done by individual journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional awards go to the organization; student awards go to individuals or teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student award submission constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Student categories include audio/video newscasts and reporting and digital reporting with specific content rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reporting categories, entries should consist of a single piece, package or series. Newscast entries should consist of a complete newscast up to 30 minutes in length. Digital entries should include digital or multimedia elements, particularly interactive elements, and should not consist solely of audio, video, or text.
